items.title: Does Learning Protein Folding Generalize to Broader Reasoning?
items.summary: Large language models rely heavily on human text, which often conveys surface answers rather than the spatial and structural logic behind them. Protein folding is a natural testbed, because one solved structure yields thousands of exactly checkable spatial and topological statements. items.title: RealCompanion: Benchmarking Human Understanding from Reasoning over Longitudinal Real-World Conversations
items.summary: A companion that talks with a person for months should come to understand them. It should remember what they said, infer who they are, and know when the past bears on the message in front of it. items.summary: Long-horizon video generation requires models to effectively leverage an increasingly long generation history. items.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have advanced robotic manipulation, but their zero-shot generalization in new tasks and environments remains limited, and their reliance on specialized training keeps them from benefiting directly from rapidly advancing general-purpose vision-language models (VLMs). items.title: On-Policy Parameter Update Direction Underlies Generalization in LLM Post-Training
items.summary: The strong generalization performance of on-policy post-training paradigms has motivated studies of their parameter update behaviors. However, these studies treat the observed behaviors only as byproducts in on-policy training, overlooking their potential to serve as optimization principles for improving the generalization of other paradigms such as supervised fine-tuning (SFT). items.title: World Action Modeling with Progressive Visual Planning
items.summary: World action models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic control by jointly predicting future visual dynamics and actions from an initial observation and instruction. items.title: Native Action-Prior Learning from Videos for World Action Models
items.summary: World action models integrate future visual dynamics with robot action prediction, but their scalability remains limited by the need for action-annotated robot trajectories. Observation-only videos contain rich evidence about interaction dynamics, but existing approaches typically use them either to pretrain visual representations that must later be adapted for control, or to infer latent actions that are subsequently grounded to robot commands.

items.summary: Masked diffusion language models (dLMs) offer a promising parallel alternative to autoregressive models for complex reasoning. items.title: SimuVerity: Benchmarking Agents for Engineering-Grade Simulink Model Generation
items.summary: Existing Simulink benchmarks mainly evaluate whether generated models compile, execute, or resemble a reference model. These criteria do not establish whether a model satisfies its engineering requirements. items.summary: Physical trajectories contain more than snapshots of a system: they also reveal how its states evolve under governing conditions. items.title: LexReward: A Taxonomy-Driven Reward Framework for Legal Language Models
items.summary: Legal language models require reward signals that capture not only answer correctness but also the multidimensional quality of legal responses. Existing reward methods, however, often rely on coarse-grained holistic judgments, providing limited domain specificity and interpretability. items.title: Science or Slop?: Benchmarking and Mitigating Scientific Slop in AI-Generated Papers
items.summary: AI-generated content, often called AI slop, is increasingly common everywhere, particularly in academia. Slop in AI-generated scientific papers, however, has more complex patterns that cannot be easily detected by existing token-based AI detectors. items.summary: As LLM agents decide on users' behalf which product to buy, which hotel to book, or which paper to cite, a preference for items from certain sources (the sites or services they come from) shapes what users receive and which sources are selected. items.summary: Long-video generation and world models have shown strong potential for interactive entertainment and embodied simulation by predicting future observations conditioned on user actions and historical memory. items.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on the responses it generates. Existing LLM multi-teacher OPD transfers what specialists predict through their output distributions. items.title: VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks
items.summary: As LLM agents undertake increasingly complex, long-horizon tasks, verifying their outputs becomes increasingly challenging. We study how verification capability can be strengthened with a fixed base model, without access to reference answers or grading rubrics at test time. items.title: Science Utopia? Closed-Loop LLM Simulation of Academic Research Ecosystems
items.summary: Scientific progress emerges from a longitudinal ecosystem in which researchers, institutions, funding agencies, collaboration networks, and the scientific literature co-evolve. items.summary: We understand little about how capabilities acquired in one language carry over to another, or what governs this transfer: evaluations rely on incomparable, saturation-prone datasets and rarely examine its determinants jointly. items.title: DEFINE: Exemplar-Guided Accent Control for Zero-Shot TTS
items.summary: Zero-shot text-to-speech (TTS) can reproduce an unseen speaker from a short reference recording, but typically entangles speaker identity and accent within the same reference. items.title: HelixWorld: A Real-time Interactive Audio-Visual World Model
items.summary: World simulation is inherently multisensory, demanding synchronized visual and acoustic dynamics in real time. Yet prevailing interactive world models remain strictly silent, focusing exclusively on visual rendering and control while overlooking the acoustic dimension. items.summary: Autoregressive (AR) video models excel at causal generation, but their reliance on next-chunk prediction confines them to a short-sighted, reactive paradigm. items.summary: Policies with similar mean returns can differ sharply in rare failures, yet estimating lower-tail conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) accurately can require many costly rollouts. items.title: Language Models that Play Chess and Explain Their Moves
items.summary: Modern chess engines are silent experts: they play at a superhuman level, but do not offer explanations for their play. On the other hand, language models (LMs) can generate plausible-sounding explanations, but their weak playing strength limits the utility of their explanations. items.summary: LLM-guided evolutionary methods, such as AlphaEvolve, have emerged as powerful approaches for challenging computational optimization problems, such as circle packing.
